questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Both exploring a new destination with great opportunities of outdoor adventures but also a good university to challenge myself academically.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy finding information as i used KU, UZH webpage and contacts and earlier students who went on exchange here. UZH was especially very helpful upon arrival with different deadlines, questions etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not any.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was alright as UZH offered by a spot at a dorm which was fairly cheap (compared to general prices in Zürich). I would recommend signing up for housing through uni as it is a great way to get housing with other students and then get to know a lot of people.
My housing was 160 students in one dorm, almost all was exchange students. It was a bit hectic at times but I was really happy about it. Very social and people are so open en keen to get to know each other. Rooms and bathrooms were alright.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very easy to commute in Zürich and the city is not that big. Public transport is expensive but works well and is worth it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
It is quite easy to sign up for courses. You have a website where you can read about the course content, the requirements and the time of the lectures. Then you just sign up on that portal. Note that some courses requires an application. Some courses are block courses (sign up early) and others are for the full semester. As an UZH student i also took a course at ETH which was super cool. Be aware that the courses' ECTS points are way lower, i had 7 courses (3 courses with 6 ECTS and 4 courses with 3 ECTS). 

You can change courses after the semester starts, so you can try out the ones your are curious about. But note that if you want to change the course can bee full before the deadline. I would recommend signing up to several, maybe more than 30 ECTS, try them out and then deregister the ones you do not want to take.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I did mostly talk to other students or texted the TA's.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Alright. I figured out late that I could take ETH courses as well, so some of them were already full. In general I would have preferred to sign up as early as possible to get the courses that get full fast and have more options available.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get an overview of the courses you like, sign up early, try them out and then deregister if you do not like them.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was alright, like at home.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was quite similar to the style at home. But the seminar classes are different, they are smaller and you discuss a lot more.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None specific.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I was expecting it to be quite expensive so I was not surprised. But you can do groceries fairly cheap and the cheap supermarkets are not far from danish prices.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The host institution have ASVZ as the sports club where you can go on trips and just do many sports. ESN also do a lot of trips and events which are cool.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I went skiing a lot which was amazing and later in the season it was more hiking. Both are really great and a good way to go on weekend trips with other students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The beautiful nature, it is amazing and easy accessible by public transport. The Jungfrau region and Appenzell region is beautiful.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, it is not far from the danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just try to mingle with people that you have courses with. I only lived with exchange students so meeting locals was mostly through courses.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There is a bit more hierarchy, so the way you approach and write the professors are way more formal.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The very structured way of handling things like residency, practicalities through uni etc.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Weekend trips are a great way to explore the nature, both winter and summer.
You are going to study some also, uni is relatively demanding.
Do uni housing of possible.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The housing experience as that was fundamental for meeting people, doing small things in our everyday life here.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The academics.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
